_meta.subject: Ticketing/issue-management architecture — generalize the binary file-vs-git backend seam (ADR-0002) shared by docs' file-bug/feature/issue skills into a 3-way backend choice (local / git / external), and add push-mode entry (watch + triage + trust gate) for backends where external actors can file items nobody in this workspace typed
prior_art: ADR-0002 — git-native execution ruling (Issues as work-item canon, PRs as merge gate) — the existing binary backend precedent this generalizes
doc-writing-rules' Phase-0 backend seam, shared verbatim by docs' file-bug/feature/issue skills
the issue skill's Phase 2 shape-routing (defect -> file-bug, feature idea -> feature, generic remainder -> task) — reused by the triage classifier
teamwork's loop-rules (autonomous continuation patterns: /goal, /loop, Stop hooks) — the mechanism the watch loop is built from
the 2026-07-17 /docs:issue seed asking for an AskUserQuestion-driven repo setup: polling or MCP watch, known-friendly auto-accept, unknown-author approval growing an allow-list
ADR-0003 (proposed, 2026-07-17) — ratifies this manifest's Axis-1 backend generalization
spec-ticketing-watch-triage (draft, 2026-07-17) — the Axis-2 watch/triage/trust contract built from v1 of this manifest
_meta.replan_diff: v1 -> v2 (2026-07-17): user asked to 'add LINEAR as an option for ticketing backend' and, when asked whether that meant menu-naming-only vs a real shipped adapter, chose a real shipped adapter. This changes ADR-0003 Decision 3 (previously: no concrete Option-C adapter ships) and adds new structure/actions v1 did not have: a concrete Linear-adapter node (n1e) alongside the generic external-interface node (n1c, now scoped to bring-your-own/other-external), plus the repo-config actions to choose and configure it. v1's n1c/a1 language ('concrete third-party implementations are out of scope') is now false for Linear specifically and is corrected below; nothing else from v1 changes.

nodes.label: ticketing/issue-management system (cross-plugin: docs capture skills + harness entry-file ruling + orchestration watch loop)
backend adapter layer
local-file adapter (docs/tickets/ TICKET files via make-doc)
git-native adapter (gh issue / PR)

external adapter interface (Jira/Notion/custom via MCP or REST, bring-your-own) — a typed contract; Linear ships as a concrete adapter (n1e) against this same interface, but OTHER third-party implementations remain repo-specific and out of this pack's scope
backend resolver — reads the repo's entry-file ruling and returns the active adapter to any caller
Linear adapter — concrete, scribe-shipped realization of the external-adapter interface via Linear's MCP server (preferred) or REST API (fallback)
repo configuration (one-time setup)
backend chooser — AskUserQuestion: Option A (local) / B (git) / C (external — Linear, scribe-shipped, or bring-your-own)
entry-mode chooser — pull-only vs watch-enabled (offered only when backend is B or C) plus, when watch is chosen, the watch mechanism (polling interval vs MCP subscription)

ruling writer — persists the backend + entry-mode choice into the entry file (CLAUDE.md routing-table row, ADR-0002-style) plus any adapter/watch config, including Linear-specific settings when n1e is chosen
on-demand capture (existing: file-bug/feature/issue skills)
capture skills' Phase 0-4 logic — mint or resume a record via the resolved backend adapter; existing behavior, only its Phase-0 backend-selection call changes from the binary check to the resolver
watch/triage (relevant only when entry-mode = watch, backend B/C)
watch loop — poll or MCP-subscribe for newly filed issues/PRs against the active backend
triage classifier — reuses the issue skill's Phase-2 shape routing (defect/feature/task) on an externally-filed item
dispatcher — on a classified, trust-cleared item, invokes n3a non-interactively to mint/resume the record
trust gate
friendlies store — durable allow-list of trusted filing accounts
trust check — looks up a filing author against n5a
approval flow — surfaces an unknown author's item to a human for approve/deny

actions.label: choose the backend for a repo, once (Option A/B/C)
choose the entry mode for a repo, once (pull-only vs watch-enabled), offered only for non-local backends
persist both choices, plus any watch config, into the entry file so they're discoverable and durable
resolve the active backend adapter at runtime for any caller
create a record in the active backend
search/dedup existing records in the active backend before minting
update an existing record (fold new detail, advance status)
capture an item and mint/resume its record, whether triggered by a human/agent invocation or by the dispatcher
watch the active backend for newly filed issues/PRs (poll or MCP-subscribe)
classify an incoming externally-filed item's shape (defect/feature/task)
check whether the filing author is a known friendly
auto-route a trusted author's item straight into capture, no human gate
hold an untrusted author's item for human review
let a human approve or deny a held item
on approval, add the author to the durable friendlies allow-list
choose the watch mechanism (polling interval vs MCP subscription) when entry mode is watch-enabled
capture and persist Linear-specific configuration (API key or MCP connector reference, workspace/team/project mapping) during repo setup
choose Linear as the concrete, scribe-shipped external adapter, as distinct from a bring-your-own external adapter against the same interface

edges.why: entry-mode is only offered once the backend choice determines it's non-local
the Linear adapter must exist as a real implementation before repo-configuration can offer it as a working choice, not just a name in a menu
the resolver reads the ruling n2c persists into the entry file
the Linear adapter reads the Linear-specific config (API key/MCP connector, workspace/team/project mapping) n2c persists
capture skills' Phase-0 call switches from the binary check to the resolver; the resolver must exist first
the watch loop consumes the entry-mode + mechanism choice n2b captures
the dispatcher routes on the classifier's shape output
the dispatcher only auto-routes after a trust-check result exists
the dispatcher hands a cleared item to capture's existing mint/resume logic
the approval flow only receives items the trust check marked unknown
an approval decision is what grows the friendlies allow-list; the store's write path depends on the approval flow producing a verdict
